battery.label: Battery
battery.description: The 12 V battery, its terminals and the earth strap, and the current that the parked car takes

alternator.label: Alternator and belt
alternator.description: The alternator, its regulator and diodes, and the auxiliary belt that drives it

starter.label: Starter motor
starter.description: The starter motor and its solenoid

fuel_pump.label: Fuel pump and filter
fuel_pump.description: The in-tank fuel pump, its relay, and the fuel filter

injectors.label: Fuel injectors
injectors.description: The fuel injectors and the fuel mixture that they give

ignition.label: Ignition
ignition.description: The ignition coils, the spark plugs and the crankshaft position sensor

cooling_fan.label: Radiator fan
cooling_fan.description: The radiator fan motor, its fuse and its relay

thermostat.label: Thermostat
thermostat.description: The thermostat that controls the coolant flow through the radiator

water_pump.label: Water pump and coolant circuit
water_pump.description: The water pump, the coolant hoses and the head gasket

brakes.label: Brakes
brakes.description: The pads, the discs, the calipers and the brake hydraulics

abs.label: ABS
abs.description: The wheel speed sensors and the ABS pump and valve module

wheel_bearings.label: Wheel bearings and drive shafts
wheel_bearings.description: The wheel bearings, the hubs and the constant velocity joints

can_bus.label: CAN bus
can_bus.description: The CAN network wires, connectors and the gateway module

ecu.label: Engine ECU
ecu.description: The engine control unit, its power supply and the immobiliser

clutch.label: Clutch
clutch.description: The clutch plate, the clutch hydraulics and the dual-mass flywheel

exhaust.label: Exhaust
exhaust.description: The exhaust pipes and boxes, the catalytic converter and the oxygen sensors

slow_crank.label: Slow crank
slow_crank.description: The engine turns slowly when the driver starts it

click_no_crank.label: Click, no crank
click_no_crank.description: One click or rapid clicks at the start, and the engine does not turn

dim_lights.label: Dim lights
dim_lights.description: The headlights or the dashboard lights are dimmer than normal

flat_after_standing.label: Flat after standing
flat_after_standing.description: The battery is flat after the car stands for a night or a few days

low_resting_voltage.label: Low resting voltage
low_resting_voltage.description: Sensor value: the resting battery voltage is less than 12.2 V

old_battery.label: Old battery
old_battery.description: Service history: the battery is more than five years old

terminal_corrosion.label: Terminal corrosion
terminal_corrosion.description: Technician note: a white or green deposit on the battery terminals

jump_start_history.label: Recent jump starts
jump_start_history.description: Service history: the car needed a jump start in the last month

battery_light.label: Battery light while driving
battery_light.description: The battery warning light comes on while the engine runs

low_charge_voltage.label: Low charge voltage
low_charge_voltage.description: Code P0562, or a charge voltage of less than 13.2 V at 2000 rpm

belt_squeal.label: Belt squeal
belt_squeal.description: A squeal from the engine bay, worst at a cold start or with the lights and heater on

flickering_lights.label: Flickering lights
flickering_lights.description: The lights flicker or pulse with the engine speed

starter_grind.label: Starter grind
starter_grind.description: A grinding or whirring noise from the starter at the start

starter_intermittent.label: Starter works sometimes
starter_intermittent.description: The starter works on some attempts and not on others

crank_no_start.label: Cranks but does not fire
crank_no_start.description: The engine turns at normal speed but does not start

no_pump_prime.label: No fuel pump hum
no_pump_prime.description: No hum from the fuel tank for two seconds when the ignition turns on

low_fuel_pressure.label: Low fuel pressure
low_fuel_pressure.description: Code P0087, or a fuel rail pressure less than the specification

lean_code.label: Lean mixture code
lean_code.description: Code P0171 or P0174, the fuel mixture is too lean

hesitation.label: Hesitation
hesitation.description: The engine hesitates or stumbles when the driver accelerates hard

power_loss.label: Loss of power
power_loss.description: The car lacks power, most at high speed or up a hill

fuel_filter_overdue.label: Fuel filter overdue
fuel_filter_overdue.description: Service history: the fuel filter change is overdue

single_misfire_code.label: One-cylinder misfire code
single_misfire_code.description: Code P0301 to P0304, a misfire on one cylinder

random_misfire_code.label: Random misfire code
random_misfire_code.description: Code P0300, misfires on more than one cylinder

rough_idle.label: Rough idle
rough_idle.description: The engine shakes or idles unevenly when the car is stationary

flashing_mil.label: Flashing engine light
flashing_mil.description: The engine warning light flashes while the car drives

high_fuel_use.label: High fuel use
high_fuel_use.description: The fuel consumption is higher than normal

plugs_overdue.label: Spark plugs overdue
plugs_overdue.description: Service history: the spark plug change is overdue

no_rpm_signal.label: No rpm signal
no_rpm_signal.description: Code P0335, or the rpm reads zero while the engine cranks

overheat_gauge.label: Overheats
overheat_gauge.description: The temperature gauge goes into the red, or a coolant temperature warning comes on

overheat_in_traffic.label: Overheats in traffic
overheat_in_traffic.description: The engine overheats when the car is stationary or in slow traffic

overheat_on_road.label: Overheats at speed
overheat_on_road.description: The engine overheats at a steady speed on the open road

coolant_temp_high.label: High coolant temperature
coolant_temp_high.description: Code P0217, or a coolant temperature of more than 110 °C

fan_not_running.label: Fan does not run
fan_not_running.description: Technician note: the radiator fan does not run when the engine is hot

heater_cold.label: Cold heater
heater_cold.description: The heater blows cold or only warm air

slow_warm_up.label: Slow warm-up
slow_warm_up.description: The temperature gauge stays low or takes a long time to rise

p0128_code.label: Thermostat code
p0128_code.description: Code P0128, the coolant temperature stays below the thermostat temperature

coolant_loss.label: Coolant loss
coolant_loss.description: The coolant level drops between top-ups

coolant_puddle.label: Coolant puddle
coolant_puddle.description: A pink, blue or green puddle under the front of the car

sweet_smell.label: Sweet smell
sweet_smell.description: A sweet smell of coolant near the car or in the cabin

white_smoke.label: White smoke
white_smoke.description: Thick white smoke with a sweet smell from the exhaust

brake_squeal.label: Brake squeal or grind
brake_squeal.description: A squeal or a metal grind when the driver brakes

brake_vibration.label: Brake vibration
brake_vibration.description: The pedal or the steering wheel shakes when the driver brakes

pull_when_braking.label: Pulls when braking
pull_when_braking.description: The car pulls to one side when the driver brakes

hot_wheel.label: Hot wheel
hot_wheel.description: Technician note: one wheel is much hotter than the others after a drive

burning_smell.label: Burning smell
burning_smell.description: A burning smell after a drive, a hill start or a tow

soft_pedal.label: Soft brake pedal
soft_pedal.description: The brake pedal is soft or spongy, or goes down too far

brake_warning_light.label: Brake warning light
brake_warning_light.description: The red brake warning light is on

low_brake_fluid.label: Low brake fluid
low_brake_fluid.description: Technician note: the brake fluid level is below the minimum mark

abs_light.label: ABS light
abs_light.description: The ABS warning light is on

wheel_speed_code.label: Wheel speed code
wheel_speed_code.description: Code C0035 to C0050, a wheel speed sensor signal fault

traction_light.label: Traction control light
traction_light.description: The traction or stability control light is on

wheel_hum.label: Wheel hum
wheel_hum.description: A hum or drone from one wheel that rises with the road speed

click_on_turns.label: Click on turns
click_on_turns.description: A click or a knock from a front wheel on full lock

split_boot.label: Split drive shaft boot
split_boot.description: Technician note: a split drive shaft boot, and grease on the wheel arch

lost_comm_code.label: Lost communication code
lost_comm_code.description: Code U0100 to U0155, a module lost communication on the bus

many_warning_lights.label: Many warning lights
many_warning_lights.description: Several warning lights come on at the same time, or the gauges drop to zero

no_scan_link.label: No scan tool link
no_scan_link.description: The scan tool cannot connect to the engine ECU

security_light.label: Security light
security_light.description: The key or security light flashes on the dashboard

water_ingress.label: Water ingress
water_ingress.description: Technician note: water in a footwell, or corrosion at a connector

revs_no_speed.label: Revs without speed
revs_no_speed.description: The engine revs rise but the road speed does not, in a high gear

hard_gear_change.label: Hard gear change
hard_gear_change.description: The gears are hard to engage or grind, most at a standstill

clutch_pedal_floor.label: Clutch pedal to the floor
clutch_pedal_floor.description: The clutch pedal goes to the floor or stays down

idle_rattle.label: Rattle at idle
idle_rattle.description: A rattle from the gearbox area at idle that stops when the clutch pedal is down

pull_away_judder.label: Judder when pulling away
pull_away_judder.description: The car shudders when it pulls away in first gear

loud_exhaust.label: Loud exhaust
loud_exhaust.description: A loud exhaust, or a tick or blow at a cold start

cat_code.label: Catalyst code
cat_code.description: Code P0420, the catalytic converter efficiency is below the threshold

rotten_egg_smell.label: Rotten egg smell
rotten_egg_smell.description: A smell of rotten eggs from the exhaust

o2_code.label: Oxygen sensor code
o2_code.description: Code P0130 to P0141, an oxygen sensor circuit or response fault

flat_battery.label: Flat battery
flat_battery.description: The battery is healthy but has too little charge to turn the starter
fix: Measure the resting voltage across the battery terminals with the engine off.
Connect a smart charger and charge the battery to 12.6 V or more.
Do a load test on the charged battery.
Start the engine and measure the charge voltage at 2000 rpm, 13.8 V to 14.7 V.
Ask the customer about short trips or lights left on, and record the answer.

battery_end_of_life.label: Battery at end of life
battery_end_of_life.description: The battery no longer holds a charge, so it fails a load test even after a full charge
fix: Charge the battery fully and do a load test to confirm the failure.
Connect a memory saver to the diagnostic socket.
Disconnect the negative terminal, then the positive terminal, and remove the clamp.
Install a new battery with the correct capacity and cold-crank rating.
Connect the positive terminal, then the negative terminal.
Register the new battery with the diagnostic tool if the car has a battery monitor.
Measure the charge voltage at 2000 rpm, 13.8 V to 14.7 V.

battery_terminals.label: Corroded or loose battery terminals
battery_terminals.description: Corrosion or a loose clamp at the battery terminals or the earth strap blocks the current
fix: Disconnect the negative terminal first, then the positive terminal.
Clean the posts and the clamps with a terminal brush and a baking soda solution.
Examine the cables and the earth strap for corrosion under the insulation.
Replace a clamp or a cable that has corrosion under the insulation.
Connect the positive terminal first, then the negative terminal, and tighten to the torque value.
Apply terminal protection grease.
Do a start test and measure the voltage drop across each connection, 0.2 V maximum.

parasitic_drain.label: Parasitic drain
parasitic_drain.description: A circuit takes current while the car is parked and makes the battery go flat
fix: Charge the battery fully.
Lock the car and wait until the control units go to sleep, approximately 30 minutes.
Connect a clamp meter to the battery negative cable and measure the current.
Remove fuses one at a time and find the circuit that stops the drain.
Repair or replace the part on that circuit.
Measure the sleep current again, 50 mA maximum.

alternator_failure.label: Alternator failure
alternator_failure.description: The alternator or its regulator gives too little or too much charge voltage
fix: Measure the charge voltage at 2000 rpm with the lights and the fan on.
Disconnect the battery negative terminal.
Release the belt tension and remove the auxiliary belt from the alternator pulley.
Disconnect the alternator cables and remove the alternator.
Install the new alternator and connect the cables.
Install the belt, then connect the battery negative terminal.
Measure the charge voltage again, 13.8 V to 14.7 V.

aux_belt_slip.label: Slipping auxiliary belt
aux_belt_slip.description: The auxiliary belt is worn, glazed or loose, so it slips on the alternator pulley
fix: Examine the belt for cracks, glazing and missing ribs.
Examine the tensioner and the idler pulleys for noise and play.
Release the tensioner and remove the belt.
Replace the tensioner if it has play or a weak spring.
Install a new belt on the correct routing.
Run the engine with full electrical load and listen for a squeal.

alternator_diode_leak.label: Leaking alternator diode
alternator_diode_leak.description: A defective rectifier diode lets current flow back through the alternator while the car is parked
fix: Charge the battery fully.
Measure the sleep current with a clamp meter on the battery negative cable.
Disconnect the alternator B+ lead and measure the sleep current again.
Do an AC ripple test at the battery with the engine at 2000 rpm, 0.5 V AC maximum.
Replace the alternator or its rectifier.
Measure the sleep current again, 50 mA maximum.

starter_motor_worn.label: Worn starter motor
starter_motor_worn.description: The brushes, the bearings or the armature of the starter are worn, so it turns slowly or grinds
fix: Disconnect the battery negative terminal.
Remove the starter supply cable and the solenoid trigger wire.
Remove the starter motor mounting bolts and remove the starter motor.
Examine the flywheel ring gear for damaged teeth.
Install the new starter motor and tighten the bolts to the torque value.
Connect the cables and the battery negative terminal.
Do five start tests and listen for a clean engagement.

starter_solenoid.label: Starter solenoid failure
starter_solenoid.description: The solenoid contacts are burnt, so the solenoid clicks but sends no current to the starter motor
fix: Measure the voltage at the solenoid trigger terminal while the key is at start.
Measure the voltage at the motor terminal of the solenoid during the same attempt.
Disconnect the battery negative terminal.
Remove the starter motor.
Replace the solenoid, or the starter assembly if the solenoid is not a separate part.
Install the starter and tighten the bolts to the torque value.
Connect the battery and do five start tests.

fuel_pump_failed.label: Fuel pump failure
fuel_pump_failed.description: The in-tank fuel pump does not supply fuel pressure, so the engine cranks but does not fire
fix: Examine the fuel pump fuse and relay, and replace a defective part.
Connect a fuel pressure gauge to the fuel rail and measure the pressure at ignition on.
Release the fuel pressure and disconnect the battery negative terminal.
Remove the rear seat base or the access cover over the pump.
Replace the fuel pump module and install a new seal.
Connect the battery, turn the ignition on and examine the pump for leaks.
Measure the fuel pressure again and do a start test.

fuel_pump_weak.label: Weak fuel pump
fuel_pump_weak.description: The fuel pump runs but cannot hold the fuel pressure at high load
fix: Connect a fuel pressure gauge and measure the pressure at idle and at full load.
Measure the pump delivery volume in 30 s.
Release the fuel pressure and disconnect the battery negative terminal.
Remove the access cover and replace the fuel pump module with a new seal.
Connect the battery and examine the pump for leaks.
Measure the fuel pressure at full load on a road test.

fuel_filter_clogged.label: Clogged fuel filter
fuel_filter_clogged.description: A blocked fuel filter lets the fuel pressure fall at high load
fix: Release the fuel pressure.
Disconnect the battery negative terminal.
Remove the fuel filter and catch the fuel in a container.
Install the new filter with the flow arrow in the correct direction.
Connect the battery and turn the ignition on to prime the system.
Examine the filter connections for leaks.
Measure the fuel pressure at full load during a road test.

injector_clogged.label: Clogged injectors
injector_clogged.description: Deposits restrict the injectors, so all cylinders get too little fuel
fix: Read the fuel trims at idle and at 2500 rpm.
Do a smoke test on the intake to find a vacuum leak.
Remove the fuel rail and the injectors.
Do a flow test and clean the injectors in an ultrasonic cleaner.
Replace an injector that stays below 90 percent of its rated flow.
Install the injectors with new seals and clear the fuel trims.
Do a road test and read the fuel trims again, within 10 percent.

injector_stuck.label: Stuck injector
injector_stuck.description: One injector sticks open or closed, so one cylinder misfires
fix: Read the misfire codes and find the cylinder.
Do an injector balance test.
Release the fuel pressure and disconnect the battery negative terminal.
Remove the defective injector.
Install the new injector with new seals.
Code the injector to the ECU with the diagnostic tool if the ECU requires it.
Clear the codes and do a road test under load.

ignition_coil.label: Ignition coil failure
ignition_coil.description: One coil gives a weak or no spark, so one cylinder misfires
fix: Read the misfire codes and find the cylinder.
Disconnect the connector of the coil on that cylinder.
Remove the coil.
Examine the spark plug of that cylinder and replace it if it is worn.
Install the new coil and connect it.
Clear the codes and do a road test under load.

spark_plugs_worn.label: Worn spark plugs
spark_plugs_worn.description: The spark plugs are worn or fouled, so the engine misfires on more than one cylinder
fix: Remove the coils or the plug leads.
Remove the spark plugs and examine each one.
Set the gap of the new plugs to the specification.
Install the new plugs and tighten them to the torque value.
Install the coils or the plug leads.
Clear the codes and do a road test.

crank_sensor.label: Crankshaft position sensor failure
crank_sensor.description: The engine computer gets no crankshaft signal, so it gives no spark and no fuel
fix: Read the fault codes with a diagnostic tool.
Examine the sensor connector and the wires for damage and oil.
Measure the sensor resistance or the signal with an oscilloscope while the engine cranks.
Remove the sensor and clean the mounting face.
Install the new sensor with the correct air gap.
Clear the fault codes and do a start test.

radiator_fan_motor.label: Radiator fan motor failure
radiator_fan_motor.description: The radiator fan motor is seized or burnt, so the engine overheats at low speed and in traffic
fix: Examine the fan fuse and the fan relay.
Connect 12 V directly to the fan motor and see if it turns.
Examine the coolant temperature sensor and its signal.
Replace the fan motor, the relay or the sensor that is defective.
Run the engine to operating temperature and make sure that the fan starts.

fan_relay.label: Radiator fan relay failure
fan_relay.description: The fan relay does not close when the ECU commands the fan, so the fan motor gets no power
fix: Read the fan command in the live data with the engine hot.
Listen for a click from the fan relay when the ECU commands the fan.
Measure the voltage at the relay output terminal.
Replace the fan relay.
Run the engine to operating temperature and make sure that the fan starts.

thermostat_stuck_closed.label: Thermostat stuck closed
thermostat_stuck_closed.description: The thermostat does not open, so the coolant does not flow through the radiator
fix: Let the engine cool fully.
Drain the coolant into a clean container.
Remove the thermostat housing and the thermostat.
Install the new thermostat with a new seal and the correct orientation.
Fill the system with coolant and bleed the air.
Run the engine to operating temperature and feel the top hose get hot.

thermostat_stuck_open.label: Thermostat stuck open
thermostat_stuck_open.description: The thermostat does not close, so the engine does not reach its operating temperature
fix: Compare the coolant sensor value with an infrared reading at the engine.
Let the engine cool fully and drain the coolant.
Remove the thermostat housing and the thermostat.
Install the new thermostat with a new seal and the correct orientation.
Fill the system with coolant and bleed the air.
Clear code P0128 and do a road test until the gauge reaches the normal position.

water_pump_leak.label: Water pump seal leak
water_pump_leak.description: The water pump leaks at its seal, so coolant comes out at the weep hole
fix: Let the engine cool fully and drain the coolant.
Remove the drive belt or the timing belt that drives the pump.
Remove the water pump.
Clean the mounting face and install the new pump with a new gasket.
Install the belt and set its tension.
Fill the system with coolant and bleed the air.
Run the engine to operating temperature and examine the pump for leaks.

water_pump_impeller.label: Worn water pump impeller
water_pump_impeller.description: The impeller is eroded or loose on its shaft, so the coolant does not circulate at speed
fix: Measure the temperature of the top hose and the bottom hose with an infrared thermometer.
Let the engine cool fully and drain the coolant.
Remove the belt that drives the pump.
Remove the water pump and examine the impeller.
Install the new pump with a new gasket and set the belt tension.
Fill the system with coolant and bleed the air.
Do a road test at motorway speed and read the coolant temperature.

coolant_hose_leak.label: Coolant hose leak
coolant_hose_leak.description: A coolant hose or a hose clip leaks, so the coolant level falls
fix: Let the engine cool fully.
Do a pressure test on the cooling system and find the leak.
Drain the coolant to below the leak.
Replace the hose and the clips.
Fill the system with coolant and bleed the air.
Do a pressure test again for 10 minutes.

head_gasket.label: Head gasket failure
head_gasket.description: The head gasket leaks between a cylinder and a coolant passage
fix: Do a combustion leak test on the coolant.
Do a compression test and a leak-down test on each cylinder.
Tell the customer the cost of the repair and get approval before the work.
Remove the cylinder head.
Send the head for a flatness check and a pressure test.
Install the head with a new gasket and new bolts, and tighten to the torque sequence.
Fill the coolant, bleed the air and change the engine oil.
Run the engine and do a combustion leak test again.

worn_pads.label: Worn brake pads
worn_pads.description: The pad material is at or below the wear limit
fix: Lift the car and remove the wheels.
Measure the pad thickness and the disc thickness.
Push the caliper piston back and remove the old pads.
Clean the caliper carrier and apply brake grease to the contact points.
Install the new pads and the wear sensor.
Install the wheels and tighten the nuts to the torque value.
Pump the pedal until it is firm, then bed in the pads on a road test.

warped_discs.label: Warped brake discs
warped_discs.description: The brake discs have run-out or uneven thickness, so the pedal pulses when braking
fix: Lift the car and remove the wheels.
Measure the disc run-out and the thickness variation.
Remove the calipers and the discs.
Clean the hub face of rust.
Install the new discs and new pads.
Install the calipers and the wheels, and tighten to the torque values.
Bed in the pads on a road test.

sticking_caliper.label: Sticking brake caliper
sticking_caliper.description: A caliper piston or slide pin sticks, so one brake drags and gets hot
fix: Lift the car and find the wheel that drags.
Remove the wheel and the caliper.
Examine the slide pins and the piston seal.
Clean and grease the slide pins, or replace the caliper if the piston sticks.
Replace the pads and the disc if heat damaged them.
Bleed the brakes on that circuit.
Do a road test and measure the wheel temperatures.

air_in_brakes.label: Air in the brake fluid
air_in_brakes.description: Air in the hydraulic system makes the pedal soft and spongy
fix: Examine the brake pipes, the hoses and the calipers for leaks.
Fill the reservoir with new brake fluid of the correct specification.
Bleed each wheel in the sequence of the manufacturer.
Do the ABS bleed procedure with the diagnostic tool if the manual requires it.
Fill the reservoir to the maximum mark.
Make sure that the pedal is firm, then do a road test.

abs_wheel_sensor.label: ABS wheel speed sensor fault
abs_wheel_sensor.description: A wheel speed sensor or its wire gives no signal or a bad signal
fix: Read the ABS fault codes and find the wheel.
Compare the wheel speeds in the live data on a road test.
Examine the sensor wire and the connector for damage.
Measure the sensor resistance or the signal.
Clean the sensor mounting and install the new sensor.
Clear the codes and do a road test above 30 km/h.

abs_pump_module.label: ABS pump and valve module fault
abs_pump_module.description: The ABS pump motor or a valve in the hydraulic module fails
fix: Read the ABS fault codes.
Do the pump and valve actuator tests with the diagnostic tool.
Measure the supply voltage at the pump motor fuse and the module connector.
Replace the ABS module or send it for repair.
Code the module to the vehicle with the diagnostic tool.
Do the ABS bleed procedure with the diagnostic tool.
Clear the codes and make sure that the pedal is firm, then do a road test.

wheel_bearing_worn.label: Worn wheel bearing
wheel_bearing_worn.description: A wheel bearing has play or rough races, so it hums, and it can disturb the wheel speed signal
fix: Lift the car and examine each wheel for play and a rough feel.
Remove the wheel, the caliper and the disc.
Remove the hub or press out the bearing.
Install the new bearing or hub with the magnetic encoder toward the sensor.
Install the disc, the caliper and the wheel, and tighten to the torque values.
Clear the ABS codes and do a road test.

cv_joint_worn.label: Worn CV joint
cv_joint_worn.description: The outer constant velocity joint of a drive shaft is worn, most often after the boot split
fix: Do a road test in a tight circle and find the side that clicks.
Lift the car and remove the wheel.
Remove the hub nut and the drive shaft.
Install a new drive shaft, or a new joint and boot with the correct grease.
Tighten the hub nut to the torque value.
Do a road test in tight circles in both directions.

can_wiring_fault.label: CAN wiring fault
can_wiring_fault.description: Water, corrosion or chafe damages a CAN wire or connector, so the modules lose communication
fix: Read the lost-communication codes in all modules.
Measure the resistance between OBD pins 6 and 14 with the battery disconnected, 60 Ω.
Examine the connectors near water entry points for corrosion.
Divide the bus into sections and find the damaged section.
Repair the wire or replace the connector, and seal it.
Clear the codes in all modules and do a road test.

can_gateway_fault.label: Gateway module fault
can_gateway_fault.description: The gateway module does not pass messages between the CAN networks
fix: Read the codes in all modules and find the network that lost communication.
Measure the supply and the ground at the gateway module.
Replace the gateway module.
Code the new module to the vehicle with the diagnostic tool.
Clear the codes in all modules and do a road test.

ecu_power_supply.label: ECU power supply fault
ecu_power_supply.description: The ECU main relay, a fuse, or a supply or ground wire fails, so the engine ECU gets no power
fix: Measure the supply voltage at the ECU connector with the ignition on.
Examine the ECU main relay and the ECU fuses.
Measure the voltage drop on the ECU ground wires, 0.1 V maximum.
Replace the relay or the fuse, or repair the wire.
Clear the codes in all modules and do a start test.

immobiliser_fault.label: Immobiliser fault
immobiliser_fault.description: The immobiliser does not recognise the key, so the engine computer blocks the start
fix: Read the immobiliser fault codes with a diagnostic tool.
Do a start test with the spare key.
Replace the key battery if the key has one.
Examine the antenna ring around the ignition barrel and its connector.
Program the key to the vehicle with the diagnostic tool.
Clear the fault codes and do three start tests.

ecu_internal_fault.label: ECU internal fault
ecu_internal_fault.description: The engine ECU has an internal fault, so it does not respond although it has good power and a good bus
fix: Measure the supply and the ground at the ECU connector.
Examine the ECU housing and the connector for water.
Tell the customer the cost of the repair and get approval before the work.
Replace the ECU, or send it for repair.
Program the ECU and the immobiliser data with the diagnostic tool.
Clear the codes in all modules and do a road test.

clutch_slip.label: Slipping clutch
clutch_slip.description: The clutch friction plate is worn or oily, so it slips under load
fix: Do a clutch stall test in a high gear with the handbrake on.
Examine the clutch adjustment and the release system.
Remove the gearbox.
Replace the clutch plate, the pressure plate and the release bearing.
Examine the flywheel face and the crankshaft seal for oil.
Install the gearbox and do a road test.

clutch_hydraulic.label: Clutch hydraulic fault
clutch_hydraulic.description: The clutch master or slave cylinder leaks, so the clutch does not release fully
fix: Examine the fluid level in the shared reservoir.
Examine the slave cylinder and the footwell for fluid.
Replace the master cylinder or the slave cylinder that leaks.
Bleed the clutch hydraulics.
Make sure that all gears engage at a standstill, then do a road test.

dual_mass_flywheel.label: Worn dual-mass flywheel
dual_mass_flywheel.description: The springs of the dual-mass flywheel are worn, so it rattles at idle and judders when the car pulls away
fix: Measure the free rotation and the rock of the flywheel with the gearbox removed.
Remove the clutch and the flywheel.
Install a new flywheel with new bolts, and tighten to the torque sequence.
Install a new clutch kit.
Install the gearbox and do a road test.

exhaust_leak.label: Exhaust leak
exhaust_leak.description: A cracked manifold, a failed gasket or a hole lets exhaust gas out before the rear box
fix: Do a smoke test on the exhaust and find the leak.
Let the exhaust cool fully.
Replace the gasket, the section or the manifold that leaks.
Tighten the clamps and the flange nuts to the torque values.
Clear the codes and do a road test.

catalytic_converter_blocked.label: Blocked catalytic converter
catalytic_converter_blocked.description: The catalytic converter is melted or blocked, so the exhaust back pressure is too high
fix: Measure the exhaust back pressure at 2500 rpm.
Compare the inlet and outlet temperatures of the converter.
Find and repair the misfire or the fuel fault that damaged the converter.
Replace the catalytic converter with new gaskets.
Clear the codes and do a road test at full load.

o2_sensor_fault.label: Oxygen sensor fault
o2_sensor_fault.description: An oxygen sensor responds slowly or its heater fails, so the fuel control is wrong
fix: Read the oxygen sensor codes and the live sensor values.
Measure the sensor heater resistance.
Remove the sensor with a sensor socket.
Apply anti-seize compound to the thread of the new sensor and install it.
Clear the codes and do a road test.
